# Multi-statement queries, whose result is that of the last statement to run. Expected values
# follow the procedural language reference:
# https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/reference/standard-sql/procedural-language

## DECLARE and SET

# A variable without DEFAULT is NULL.
DECLARE x INT64;
SELECT x
=> null

DECLARE x ARRAY<INT64>;
SELECT x IS NULL
=> "true"

DECLARE x, y, z INT64 DEFAULT 0;
SELECT z
=> "0"

# Variable names are case-insensitive.
DECLARE Foo INT64 DEFAULT 1;
SELECT foo
=> "1"

# A DEFAULT may reference variables declared before it.
DECLARE x INT64 DEFAULT 2;
DECLARE y INT64 DEFAULT x * 3;
SELECT y
=> "6"

# A column takes precedence over a variable of the same name.
DECLARE a INT64 DEFAULT 100;
SELECT MAX(a) FROM t
=> "3"

DECLARE item DEFAULT (SELECT b FROM t WHERE a = 1);
SELECT item
=> "x"

DECLARE x INT64;
SET x = 5;
SELECT x
=> "5"

DECLARE a INT64;
DECLARE b STRING;
DECLARE c BOOL;
SET (a, b, c) = (1 + 3, 'foo', false);
SELECT a
=> "4"

DECLARE a INT64;
DECLARE b STRING;
DECLARE c BOOL;
SET (a, b, c) = (1 + 3, 'foo', false);
SELECT b
=> "foo"

DECLARE a INT64;
DECLARE b STRING;
DECLARE c BOOL;
SET (a, b, c) = (1 + 3, 'foo', false);
SELECT c
=> "false"

# The query's first column goes to the first variable, and its second to the second.
DECLARE lo, hi INT64;
SET (lo, hi) = (SELECT AS STRUCT MIN(a) AS smallest, MAX(a) AS largest FROM t);
SELECT hi
=> "3"

## Parameterized types

# Type parameters constrain what a variable takes, and a value that breaks them fails the
# assignment with an error the script may handle. Expected values follow the data types reference:
# https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/reference/standard-sql/data-types#parameterized_data_types

DECLARE x STRING(10);
SET x = "hello";
SELECT x
=> "hello"

DECLARE x STRING(10);
BEGIN
  SET x = "this string is too long";
EXCEPTION WHEN ERROR THEN
  SELECT 'failed';
END;
=> "failed"

# L counts Unicode characters in a STRING and bytes in BYTES.
DECLARE x STRING(2) DEFAULT 'あい';
SELECT x
=> "あい"

DECLARE x BYTES(2);
BEGIN
  SET x = CAST('あ' AS BYTES);
EXCEPTION WHEN ERROR THEN
  SELECT 'failed';
END;
=> "failed"

# A variable reads as a NUMERIC without type parameters.
DECLARE x NUMERIC(10) DEFAULT 12345;
DECLARE y NUMERIC(5, 2) DEFAULT 123.45;
SELECT x + y
=> "12468.45"

# A value with more than S decimal digits is rounded half up to S of them.
DECLARE x NUMERIC(5, 2) DEFAULT 1.125;
SELECT x
=> "1.13"

DECLARE x BIGNUMERIC(5, 2) DEFAULT 1.125;
SELECT x
=> "1.13"

# A value with more than P digits fails.
DECLARE x NUMERIC(5, 2);
BEGIN
  SET x = 1111;
EXCEPTION WHEN ERROR THEN
  SELECT 'failed';
END;
=> "failed"

# The type parameters of a field or an element constrain it too.
DECLARE x STRUCT<s STRING(1)>;
BEGIN
  SET x = STRUCT('ab');
EXCEPTION WHEN ERROR THEN
  SELECT 'failed';
END;
=> "failed"

DECLARE x ARRAY<BYTES(1)>;
BEGIN
  SET x = [b'a', b'ab'];
EXCEPTION WHEN ERROR THEN
  SELECT 'failed';
END;
=> "failed"

## BEGIN...END

DECLARE x INT64 DEFAULT 10;
BEGIN
  DECLARE y INT64;
  SET y = x;
  SELECT y;
END;
SELECT x;
=> "10"

## BEGIN...EXCEPTION...END

BEGIN
  SELECT 1/0;
EXCEPTION WHEN ERROR THEN
  SELECT @@error.statement_text;
END;
=> "SELECT 1/0"

# @@error.message matches the message RAISE gives.
BEGIN
  RAISE USING MESSAGE = 'oops';
EXCEPTION WHEN ERROR THEN
  SELECT @@error.message;
END;
=> "oops"

# Answers collected from BigQuery with bqanswers: a handler sees the error of a definition that
# refers to a system variable. BigQuery prefixes the message with "Query error: " and appends the
# statement's location, which the emulator does not.
BEGIN
  CREATE TEMP FUNCTION f() AS (@@dataset_id);
EXCEPTION WHEN ERROR THEN
  SELECT REGEXP_CONTAINS(@@error.message, r'^(Query error: )?Invalid reference to system variable @@dataset_id; in function f( at \[\d+:\d+\])?$');
END
=> "true"

BEGIN
  EXECUTE IMMEDIATE 'CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW scalars.system_variable_view AS SELECT @@dataset_id AS dataset_id';
EXCEPTION WHEN ERROR THEN
  SELECT REGEXP_CONTAINS(@@error.message, r'^(Query error: )?Invalid reference to system variable @@dataset_id( at \[\d+:\d+\])?$');
END
=> "true"

## CASE

DECLARE product_id INT64 DEFAULT 1;
CASE product_id
  WHEN 1 THEN
    SELECT CONCAT('Product one');
  WHEN 2 THEN
    SELECT CONCAT('Product two');
  ELSE
    SELECT CONCAT('Invalid product');
END CASE;
=> "Product one"

DECLARE target_product_id INT64 DEFAULT 2;
CASE
  WHEN EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM t WHERE a = target_product_id) THEN SELECT 'found';
  ELSE SELECT 'did not find';
END CASE;
=> "found"

## IF

DECLARE target_product_id INT64 DEFAULT 103;
IF target_product_id IS NULL THEN
  -- Do nothing.
ELSE
  SELECT CONCAT('Product ID: ', CAST(target_product_id AS STRING));
END IF;
=> "Product ID: 103"

DECLARE target_product_id INT64 DEFAULT 103;
IF EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM t WHERE a = target_product_id) THEN
  SELECT CONCAT('found product ', CAST(target_product_id AS STRING));
ELSE
  SELECT CONCAT('did not find product ', CAST(target_product_id AS STRING));
END IF;
=> "did not find product 103"

## Labels

label_1: BEGIN
  SELECT 1;
  BREAK label_1;
  SELECT 2; -- Unreached
END;
=> "1"

## Loops

DECLARE x INT64 DEFAULT 0;
LOOP
  SET x = x + 1;
  IF x >= 10 THEN
    LEAVE;
  END IF;
END LOOP;
SELECT x;
=> "10"

DECLARE x INT64 DEFAULT 0;
REPEAT
  SET x = x + 1;
  SELECT x;
  UNTIL x >= 3
END REPEAT;
=> "3"

DECLARE x INT64 DEFAULT 0;
WHILE x < 3 DO
  SET x = x + 1;
END WHILE;
SELECT x;
=> "3"

# CONTINUE returns to the start of the loop.
DECLARE x INT64 DEFAULT 0;
DECLARE n INT64 DEFAULT 0;
WHILE x < 4 DO
  SET x = x + 1;
  IF MOD(x, 2) = 0 THEN
    CONTINUE;
  END IF;
  SET n = n + 1;
END WHILE;
SELECT n;
=> "2"

# Each row is a STRUCT of the query's columns.
DECLARE total INT64 DEFAULT 0;
FOR record IN (SELECT a, b FROM t WHERE a IS NOT NULL) DO
  SET total = total + record.a;
END FOR;
SELECT total;
=> "6"

## RETURN

SELECT 1;
RETURN;
SELECT 2;
=> "1"

## Temporary tables
# Expected values follow
# https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/multi-statement-queries#temporary_tables

CREATE TEMP TABLE n AS SELECT 5 AS x;
SELECT x FROM n
=> "5"

CREATE TEMPORARY TABLE n (x INT64);
INSERT n (x) VALUES (1), (2);
UPDATE n SET x = x * 10 WHERE x = 2;
DELETE FROM n WHERE x = 1;
SELECT SUM(x) FROM n
=> "20"

# _SESSION names a temporary table explicitly.
CREATE TEMP TABLE _SESSION.n AS SELECT 6 AS x;
SELECT x FROM n
=> "6"

CREATE TEMP TABLE n AS SELECT 7 AS x;
SELECT x FROM _SESSION.n
=> "7"

# An unqualified name refers to a temporary table before a table of the default dataset.
CREATE TEMP TABLE t AS SELECT 10 AS a;
SELECT MAX(a) FROM t
=> "10"

CREATE TEMP TABLE t AS SELECT 10 AS a;
SELECT MAX(a) FROM scalars.t
=> "3"

## Transactions
# Expected behavior follows https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/transactions:
# DML changes commit or roll back together; temporary-table DDL is permitted.

CREATE TEMP TABLE tx (x INT64);
BEGIN TRANSACTION;
INSERT tx VALUES (1);
COMMIT TRANSACTION;
SELECT SUM(x) FROM tx
=> "1"

CREATE TEMP TABLE tx AS SELECT 1 AS x;
BEGIN TRANSACTION;
UPDATE tx SET x = 2 WHERE TRUE;
ROLLBACK TRANSACTION;
SELECT SUM(x) FROM tx
=> "1"

# Scalar expressions in the script see its uncommitted writes.
DECLARE n INT64;
CREATE TEMP TABLE tx (x INT64);
BEGIN TRANSACTION;
INSERT tx VALUES (7);
SET n = (SELECT SUM(x) FROM tx);
ROLLBACK TRANSACTION;
SELECT n
=> "7"

BEGIN TRANSACTION;
CREATE TEMP TABLE tx AS SELECT 3 AS x;
SELECT x FROM tx;
DROP TABLE tx;
COMMIT TRANSACTION;
SELECT 1
=> "1"

# The handler can roll back even when DuckDB aborted the transaction on a runtime error.
CREATE TEMP TABLE tx AS SELECT 1 AS x;
BEGIN
  BEGIN TRANSACTION;
  UPDATE tx SET x = 2 WHERE TRUE;
  SELECT 1 / 0;
EXCEPTION WHEN ERROR THEN
  ROLLBACK TRANSACTION;
END;
SELECT SUM(x) FROM tx
=> "1"

# A temporary SQL UDF declared before a transaction can read its uncommitted rows.
# UDF calls follow https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/user-defined-functions.
DECLARE n INT64;
CREATE TEMP TABLE tx (x INT64);
CREATE TEMP FUNCTION total() AS ((SELECT SUM(x) FROM tx));
BEGIN TRANSACTION;
INSERT tx VALUES (5);
SET n = total();
ROLLBACK TRANSACTION;
SELECT n
=> "5"

# Answers collected from BigQuery with bqanswers.
# A variable keeps a NULL array, which BigQuery returns to clients as an empty one.
DECLARE x ARRAY<INT64> DEFAULT [1];
SET x = NULL;
SELECT x IS NULL
=> "true"

# Inside a query, "NULL and empty ARRAYs are two distinct values", in a struct too.
# https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/reference/standard-sql/data-types#array_type
DECLARE x STRUCT<y ARRAY<STRING>> DEFAULT STRUCT(['a']);
SET x = STRUCT(CAST(NULL AS ARRAY<STRING>));
SELECT x.y IS NULL
=> "true"

DECLARE x ARRAY<INT64> DEFAULT [1];
SET x = [];
SELECT x IS NULL
=> "false"

## EXECUTE IMMEDIATE
# https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/reference/standard-sql/procedural-language#execute_immediate,
# whose examples set y to 5 and fill Books with four rows, the earliest from 1599.

DECLARE y INT64;
DECLARE z INT64;
DECLARE book_name STRING DEFAULT 'Ulysses';
DECLARE book_year INT64 DEFAULT 1922;
DECLARE first_date INT64;
EXECUTE IMMEDIATE "SELECT ? * (? + 2)" INTO y USING 1, 3;
EXECUTE IMMEDIATE "SELECT @a * (@b + 2)" INTO z USING 1 as a, 3 as b;
EXECUTE IMMEDIATE
  "CREATE TEMP TABLE Books (title STRING, publish_date INT64)";
EXECUTE IMMEDIATE
  "INSERT INTO Books (title, publish_date) VALUES('Hamlet', 1599)";
EXECUTE IMMEDIATE
  "INSERT INTO Books (title, publish_date) VALUES(?, ?)"
  USING book_name, book_year;
EXECUTE IMMEDIATE
  "INSERT INTO Books (title, publish_date) VALUES(@name, @year)"
  USING 1815 as year, "Emma" as name;
EXECUTE IMMEDIATE
  CONCAT(
    "INSERT INTO Books (title, publish_date)", "VALUES('Middlemarch', 1871)"
  );
EXECUTE IMMEDIATE "SELECT MIN(publish_date) FROM Books LIMIT 1" INTO first_date;
SELECT TO_JSON_STRING(ARRAY(SELECT AS STRUCT title, publish_date, y, z, first_date FROM Books
  ORDER BY publish_date))
=> "[{\"title\":\"Hamlet\",\"publish_date\":1599,\"y\":5,\"z\":5,\"first_date\":1599},{\"title\":\"Emma\",\"publish_date\":1815,\"y\":5,\"z\":5,\"first_date\":1599},{\"title\":\"Middlemarch\",\"publish_date\":1871,\"y\":5,\"z\":5,\"first_date\":1599},{\"title\":\"Ulysses\",\"publish_date\":1922,\"y\":5,\"z\":5,\"first_date\":1599}]"

# The statement's result is the result of the whole statement, INTO sets every variable to NULL
# for no rows, and a variable may be both in INTO and in USING.
EXECUTE IMMEDIATE "SELECT @a * (@b + 2)" USING 1 as a, 3 as b
=> "5"

DECLARE x INT64 DEFAULT 1;
EXECUTE IMMEDIATE "SELECT 2 FROM UNNEST([])" INTO x;
SELECT x
=> null

DECLARE y INT64 DEFAULT 1;
EXECUTE IMMEDIATE "SELECT ? + 1" INTO y USING y;
SELECT y
=> "2"

## Dataset system variables
# SET and name resolution follow the system variables reference:
# https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/reference/system-variables

SET @@dataset_id = 'scalars';
SELECT @@dataset_id
=> "scalars"

SET @@dataset_project_id = 'example-project';
SELECT @@dataset_project_id
=> "example-project"

DECLARE dataset STRING DEFAULT 'scalars';
SET @@DATASET_ID = dataset;
SELECT MAX(a) FROM t
=> "3"

DECLARE n INT64;
SET @@dataset_id = CONCAT('sca', 'lars');
SET n = (SELECT MAX(a) FROM t);
SELECT n
=> "3"

SET @@dataset_id = 'scalars';
EXECUTE IMMEDIATE 'SELECT MAX(a) FROM t'
=> "3"

SET @@dataset_project_id = 'example-project';
SET @@dataset_project_id = NULL;
SELECT @@dataset_project_id IS NULL
=> "true"

SET @@dataset_project_id = 'example-project';
SET @@dataset_project_id = NULL;
SET @@dataset_id = 'scalars';
SELECT MAX(a) FROM t
=> "3"

SET @@dataset_id = 'no_such_dataset';
SELECT MAX(a) FROM scalars.t
=> "3"

# A temporary table still takes precedence over the selected default dataset.
CREATE TEMP TABLE t AS SELECT 9 AS a;
SET @@dataset_id = 'scalars';
SELECT MAX(a) FROM t
=> "9"

# Assignments must have the documented STRING type.
SET @@dataset_id = 123;
SELECT 1
=> error:

SET @@dataset_project_id = TRUE;
SELECT 1
=> error:

# Answers collected from BigQuery with bqanswers: NULL clears the default dataset.
SET @@dataset_id = 'example_dataset'; SELECT @@dataset_id;
SET @@dataset_id = NULL; SELECT @@dataset_id
=> null

SET @@dataset_id = 'scalars';
SET @@dataset_id = NULL;
SELECT a FROM t
=> error contains: Table "t" must be qualified with a dataset (e.g. dataset.table).
